summary: Lovett Lookout in the Brazeau Forest: four radio stations reported in 1938 with Lovett planned as a fifth, a lumber cabin completed in 1946, a road in 1948 and a 10.7 m (35 ft) steel tower in the year to March 1949.

facts.design: Steel tower of 10.7 m (35 ft) built in the year to 31 March 1949; lumber cabin with a brick chimney, completed by 1946, at the same lookout

access.note: No source read describes public access today. In 1948 the archive says a car could reach the tower by a graded road.

events.note: Four radio lookout stations reported in operation; a fifth was to be built at Lovett
Work began on a lumber cabin to replace the original log lookout building
Lumber cabin completed; planned as quarters for a married lookout man
Wagon road to the lookout graded so a car could drive to the tower
35-ft steel tower built by reserve field staff, per the annual report for the year ended 31 March 1949

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The archive gives a 35-ft (10.7 m) steel tower built in 1949. The brief's record gives 30 m for the present structure, and dates it to 2017. No source read names a 2017 build or a 30 m height, so height_m is left out of facts and the 1949 tower is described as the 1949 tower.

notes_for_editor: The archive is the only Lovett-specific source and it quotes annual reports and a 1938 newspaper, but the original reports were not read. The archive's year headings (1945, 1946, 1948, 1949) are used as given; the quoted annual reports cover the years ended 31 March 1946, 1947 and 1949, so the 1946 cabin entry comes from the report for the year ended 31 March 1947. Nothing after 1949 is sourced. The brief's record says staffed March to October, closed access, 30 m height, steel, and a 2017 present structure; none of these is verified, and a 2017 replacement would explain the gap with the 1949 35-ft tower. Elevation 1477 m not used. Agency is the brief's Alberta Wildfire, supported only by the Alberta-wide statement. Searches used: 2. Page reads: about 3.
